rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and Tables 1, 4-6 - the authors collected their own canopy reflectance (172 plant spectra, FieldSpec 3) at three cotton fields in Andhra Pradesh and Tamilnadu in 2010-11, with leaf chlorophyll and RWC measurements, and regressed indices against visually graded leafhopper severity.
rows.notes: Q2 no: the study only shows that hyperspectral bands and new Leafhopper Indices (LHI 2, LHI 4; R2 0.461-0.850 across fields, Table 6) correlate with leafhopper damage grades on individual plants (plant-level ground spectroradiometry, not area mapping). It does not test whether this detection leads to any action by farmers or to prevention of further damage; the pest-control effect in the passage is only a downstream possibility (Discussion mentions mapped variations being amenable to site-specific control, citing Willers and Riggins 2010, but no such test here). Supports only the detection precondition, so upstream = true. Study-level observations not scored because Q2 is no: single season, three fields, two locations, one growth stage (boll maturity); Chl/RWC not measured in Field 3; authors note inconsistency of index performance across fields and possible edaphic/weather/cultivar influences; CV and LSD reported for Chl/RWC (Table 5) and SD for reflectance t-tests (Table 4).

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a ground-based hyperspectral detection study of leafhopper stress in cotton; it contains no evaluation of pest control or damage prevention outcomes.
